project_title: Graphic Novel Script Adapter Needed — Create Polished Sample for Crowdfunding

project_metadata.job_title: Graphic Novel Script Adapter Needed — Create Polished Sample for Crowdfunding
project_metadata.job_description:
I’m looking for a writer experienced in graphic novels, comics, or sequential storytelling to adapt a portion of my completed screenplay into a polished sample script for a future crowdfunding campaign.

This job is for a paid sample only (fixed price: $100). If the sample works well, there will be an opportunity to continue with the full graphic novel script.

What I need:

Adapt a selected section of my screenplay into a comic/graphic novel script format
Break the material into pages, panels, dialogue, captions, and visual direction
Maintain pacing, clarity, and strong visual storytelling
Deliver a clean, professional script sample suitable for showing to artists and potential backers

What I will provide:

The full screenplay
Character notes and tone/style references
The specific scene/sequence to adapt for the sample

Ideal experience:

Comic book or graphic novel writing
Screenplay adaptation
Panel‑by‑panel scripting
Storyboarding or sequential art familiarity (a plus)

This sample will be used to help pitch the project and secure funding. If we’re a good fit, there will be ongoing paid work as the project moves into full production.

Please include relevant writing samples, especially any comic or graphic novel work.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001].

Thanks for replying so quickly. I'll do my best to address your questions.

1. My initial thought was to begin at the start and continue as far into the story as I could. However, if you would rather have me concentrate on a particular section, I can focus on that instead.

2. The sample folder I shared shows the script style I normally use. My recommendation is to organize every page in a panel format. I occasionally indicate where captions should go, but I generally leave the exact placement of dialogue balloons and similar elements to the artist.

3. Because I would be adapting your script, my main influence over pacing and structure would come from choosing how many panels, or how much room on the page, each moment receives. I expect those decisions to be reasonably self-explanatory, though I can explain anything you ask about after the writing is complete. Including explanatory notes would require additional time and would therefore raise my rate for the larger project.

I look forward to your response.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Great! Thanks for getting back to me. I am continuing to assess all candidates today and expect to decide by the end of my day (my time). If you have any questions, please let me know.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
I have one last question... how much time would you need to finish this sample project?
Thanks!
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Provided I can begin tomorrow, my goal would be to return the script to you on Friday. This schedule would give me time between the first and second draft while also leaving room to address any questions that arise.
Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I would like to proceed with the 12-page sample from you. Please tell me if you want to accept, and I will send over the contract. Its terms will be what we discussed in our messages. Let me know if you have any questions; if not, I will send it shortly. Thanks!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I have attached several additional files that provide more information. Please tell me if you have questions or if there is anything further you need from me. I am available throughout the day and, if necessary, at night. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Great. It appears that you have funded the project already, so I will start working on it in the morning. I'll contact you if any questions arise, and regardless, I'll try to send an update at the end of the day tomorrow.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
A quick update: I made solid progress today and developed a provisional breakdown that reaches Tom's meeting with Apollonia on comic page 12. I may determine that the pacing is too fast if some beats require additional room to breathe, but that is something I will have to assess while working.
There are two questions—or, more accurately, two possible approaches to the script—that I would like to confirm with you:
1. In several spots, I am considering adapting portions of the scene descriptions into "voice over" captions.
2. To save page space and improve efficiency, I may omit a few brief exchanges. One example is at the bottom of page 23, when Carter tells Tom that he is invited to the dinner Tom attends in the next scene.
Before doing so, I wanted to ask whether departures from the script on that scale are acceptable, or whether you want the comic to follow the screenplay line-for-line. Please share your thoughts.
Thanks.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
You have carte blanche on this. Because it is a sample piece, I will rely on your judgement.
Tell me if you need anything from me.
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: One additional heads-up: I will be away from my desk for the majority of tomorrow. If you send any questions, I will respond as soon as I am able.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: This is nice work! I will contact you if anything further is needed. Please let me know if you are comfortable leaving the contract open for a little longer. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Absolutely! There is no reason to close the job at this stage.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_001]!
What would your total quote be for 80-85 pages?
Thanks!
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi! It's good to hear from you again.
Could you tell me how many episodes/screenplay pages you expect the 85 comic pages to encompass? Knowing that will help me estimate the time required.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The original book was split into 5 parts. For the first graphic novel, I am considering the first two parts. I can forward the files to you later this evening. I am currently finalizing production costs, and the crowdfunding will launch on Monday. I would appreciate receiving your quote before then. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Thank you. I'll review the files already in my possession, along with anything else you choose to send, and calculate the estimate. I will try to provide it this evening; if I cannot, I will send it on Sunday.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I ran some calculations using the material I have already written.
Just to confirm, do you mean 85 screenplay pages or 85 comic pages? My adaptation worked out to an approximate 2:1 ratio of screenplay pages to comic pages.
Assuming part 2 is roughly as long as episode 1, which I worked from, parts 1 and 2 would total around 40-45 comic pages. I could price that work at $350 with a schedule of 2 weeks. If I am able to reuse 12 pages from the sample script, perhaps with minor revisions and page reflowing, I could reduce the price to $275.
I can also produce 80-85 comic pages, but that would likely mean covering a larger portion of the story, presumably through episode 3 or 4. For that scope, my proposal would be $675 with a 4-week turnaround, or $600 even if the 12 pages of sample script are reused.
Please let me know which option is more consistent with what you have in mind and whether these terms work for you.
Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The current estimate is 85 pages of comic. I have included the next two scripts here. I believe I also sent you a version of the novel, which is divided into three sections. That may serve as a better source than the scripts. Please review everything and tell me what you think.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I have also allocated $1500 in my budget for this service. Although I appreciate your quote, I believe that amount would compensate your time more appropriately. Let me know if you have questions, and I will update you when I have news. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
In that event, thank you very much. At that rate, I can devote more time to determining the strongest way to present all of the material instead of adhering so closely to the screenplay.

Do you want me to begin next week, or should I hold off until you say "go?"

I can commit to writing 80-85 comic pages. After reviewing the next two episodes and the novel, I will decide how much of the story can fit within that length. While doing so, should I structure the pacing around eventually scripting the remainder of the story? In other words, do you want this portion to feel self-contained, or should it emphasize leaving readers wondering, "What's next?"

Thanks,
[FREELANCER_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The listing will be posted on Monday. Would you have any issue with me naming you as the project's scripter, or using whatever title you would prefer?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I have no objection, and my preferred credit is Corodon Fuller.

If you would rather avoid additional bidders, you can create the next job as a follow-up to this one, or I can set it up.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I will create an additional milestone, but please remember that I am counting on funding this through Kickstarter. Fingers crossed.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: To confirm, is this portion of the job dependent on the Kickstarter receiving funding?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Yes. I thought I had made that clear. Would that affect whether you remain involved?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I had understood that this material would help secure crowdfunding, rather than that its own funding had not yet been secured.
Unfortunately, I cannot accept spec work through this site, and even if I could, this project is too large for me to undertake that way.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I am sorry for the misunderstanding. I am still hoping to obtain funding, and the sample I paid for was part of that effort. If the campaign succeeds, I will proceed with the project. I am not requesting any work from you at this time. However, if you prefer to withdraw, please tell me ASAP.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I may have interpreted the situation incorrectly, and I apologize if my response seemed abrupt. Once the funding is available, I will be glad to move forward with the work, and I can wait to begin while you conduct the Kickstarter campaign.
Best of luck with it. I look forward to hearing that the campaign succeeded.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: No worries! Once the link is live, I will share it with you. If you have a brief bio, I can include that in the listing, but the choice is yours.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Here is the link. The pre-launch takes place tomorrow, followed by the full launch on Wednesday. You are welcome to share it.
[URL_001]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: That's fantastic. Thank you, and I wish you the best of luck with it.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Unfortunately, the results were not as strong as I had hoped. Thank you for your involvement and the work you put in. I will close the contract tomorrow, and I will of course leave you a top-notch review. I appreciate the time you devoted to this.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I'm sorry it didn't work out as hoped. I have enjoyed working with you and wish you every success with your future projects. If you need a writer again, please remember me.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hey [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
The artist assigned to this project has volunteered to produce additional artwork gratis and would like me to run the kickstarter another time. With that in mind, if you are okay with it, I will leave the contract open. I will let you know whenever the situation changes.
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: That's fine. If anything else is needed, please let me know, and I will watch for further updates.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_001],
There is not much to report right now. At present, I am considering a schedule that would have this launched again by the end of July.
Thank you again for all your help!
[CLIENT_NAME_002]

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: This project has now been placed on hold indefinitely, so I am going to close the contract. Thank you for your time; I will leave you excellent feedback. If there is ever anything you need, please let me know.
